description: First-order linear homogeneous ODE with constant coefficient: y' + ay = 0, solved by separation of variables to give the general solution y = Ae^{-ax}. Includes a classification drill (which equations are/aren't of this separable form) and two fully-worked examples.

source.description: Cambodian BAC II grade-12 differential-equations lesson chapter (PHANKIMSIE booklet) — lesson definitions, theorems, and fully worked examples, photographed pages

lessons.title: Recognizing y' + ay = 0 form (not every ODE is directly solvable this way)
lessons.statement_latex: \text{ក. } y' = -2 + y \qquad \text{ខ. } y' - y = 4 \qquad \text{គ. } \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y-1}{xy} - x
solution_steps: \text{ក. } y' = -2+y \iff y' - y = -2 \text{ is of the form } y' + ay = p(x) \text{ (homogeneous constant-coefficient form } y'+ay=0 \text{ does not apply directly since RHS} \neq 0\text{).}
\text{ខ. } y' - y = 4 \text{ is likewise non-homogeneous (constant RHS).}
\text{គ. } \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y-1}{xy} - x \text{ is not of the linear constant-coefficient form at all.}
